name: Eric Swalwell
role: U.S. Representative from California (2013-2026); 2019 presidential and 2026 California gubernatorial candidate
summary: Swalwell is a mainstream Democrat best known for advocating a federal ban and buyback of assault weapons. He has backed a public option and coverage for all, the Green New Deal, higher taxes on the wealthy, abortion rights and LGBT equality, and in 2026 campaigned on abolishing ICE and taxing corporations. Much of his available record is from his 2019 presidential campaign.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted yes on the Women's Health Protection Act (2021), the Ensuring Access to Abortion Act (2022) and the Equal Access to Contraception for Veterans Act, and no on bills to prohibit taxpayer-funded abortions.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Voted yes on the 2014 resolutions condemning Russia's violation of Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and on H.R. 4278 supporting Ukraine's territorial integrity.

ban-cartels.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said super PACs buy influence and game the political system, and backed campaign-spending disclosure and small-donor matching.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He proposes reparative wealth-building programs for descendants of slavery.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

death-penalty.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-14): the earlier answer rested on an OnTheIssues entry whose source is a Politico compilation (2020 Dems on the Issues, July 2019), not his own words; the Politico page and a statement of his own could not be found (see notFound).

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He pledges to protect and expand Medi-Cal and income supports, but also criticises homelessness spending that does not measure results; he does not address the dependency claim, so -1.

decide-locally.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

democracy-best.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Supported the Green New Deal and the Paris accord, while saying jobs should be protected.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He promises renewed allied commitments and restoration of NATO ties.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Voted yes on the Equality Act (2021) and the Voting Rights Advancement Act (2019, 2021).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted no on the Keystone XL pipeline bills (2013-2015) and on the Offshore Energy and Jobs Act (2013).

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-14): the earlier answer cited OnTheIssues, whose source is a 2019 New York Times candidate questionnaire that could not be opened (see notFound); his House issues pages mention only nuclear research and development, not construction of plants.

family-wage.rationale: His resolution explicitly supports family-sustaining wages.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted no in April 2018 on the joint resolution proposing a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution.

free-public-college.rationale: He backs free community college for the first two years (with a show-you-work condition) and debt-free university through work-study and service, not tuition-free public universities; mixed, so 0 low.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voted yes on the Equality Act in 2021, which bars discrimination in public accommodations and employment.

future-generations.rationale: His resolution commits to a sustainable environment for future generations.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Voted yes on the Equality Act (2021), which bars discrimination on the basis of gender identity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His resolution requires Indigenous consent for decisions affecting traditional territories.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said Jewish people deserve a state after the Holocaust and that Israel has a right to defend itself, while opposing the Netanyahu government and criticising settler violence.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He insists the Constitution takes precedence over the Ten Commandments.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted yes on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and Enhanced Background Checks Act (2019, 2021) and on the 2022 Assault Weapons Ban.

means-match-ends.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

minority-language-support.rationale: He promises multilingual services, alerts and qualified sign-language interpretation.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He opposes Christian-nationalist indoctrination in schools but accepts classroom teaching of the Bible's historic value and other faiths' books, so the view is mixed in wording; low.

open-borders.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

participatory-democracy.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

party-controls-media.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

racial-franchise.rationale: Voted yes on the Voting Rights Advancement Act (2019) and the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act (2021).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted yes on the Raise the Wage Act in July 2019, which phases the federal minimum wage up to $15.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Backed raising both high-skill and family-based visa caps and supported the DREAM Act and the 2013 immigration reform bill.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He proposes a mandatory independent AI audit with liability, conditions state support on labor standards and backs corporate tax changes; these are several specific measures, not a general tightening, so +1.

rehabilitation.rationale: He favors treatment, diversion and meaningful reintegration over unnecessary incarceration.

religious-nation.rationale: He explicitly rejects Christian nationalism and an exclusively Christian country.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted yes on the Equality Act (2021) and on the Respect for Marriage Act in July and December 2022.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted no on the Scholarships for Opportunity and Results (SOAR) Act reauthorization, which funds private school vouchers in Washington, D.C., in October 2015 and April 2016.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separate-church-state.rationale: He explicitly advocates secular government separated from every faith.

separated-powers.rationale: He argues that Congress must hold the president accountable and investigate; he does not state the principle of divided power itself, so +1.

social-market-economy.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Voted for both articles of impeachment against President Trump in December 2019 and for the January 2021 article.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He calls for California to be an active market-shaper using purchasing, grants and incentives with tech and life-science firms; this is a gubernatorial plan for conditional partnerships, so +1.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Proposed no-interest federal student loans, tax-free employer contributions toward workers' loans and debt-free college; did not call for broad cancellation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He criticised the Speaker's wish for a country free from dissent and defended his own critics' right to speak; this is a single episode, so -1.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted yes on passage of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act (April 2024), which reauthorizes FISA Section 702 without a warrant requirement, and no on the amendment requiring warrants and on the Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-14): the earlier answer rested on an OnTheIssues summary of his cosponsoring the Sugar Reform Act, a bill adjusting sugar program quotas, which fits either answer on tariffs against foreign competition; his roll calls hold no tariff vote.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted no on the 2015 Death Tax Repeal Act, keeping the estate tax; the vote does not show support for heavy taxation of large inheritances.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said the wealthy should pay more taxes, backed raising the payroll tax cap, and in 2026 proposed a new corporate tax.

unions-good.rationale: Voted yes on the Protecting the Right to Organize Act in February 2020.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cosponsored Medicare for All in 2019 and said he wants coverage for all, with a public option and private plans kept; called Medicare for All 'the obvious solution' but opposed eliminating private insurers.

voter-id.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-14): the earlier answer rested on OnTheIssues' gloss on his cosponsoring the Voting Rights Amendment Act, whose text does not mention photo ID; his no votes on the SAVE Acts (2024, 2025) concern proof of citizenship.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He promises to restore Medi-Cal coverage regardless of immigration status; this covers one program, not welfare benefits generally, so -1.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted no in March 2013 on H.R. 890, which would bar waivers of the TANF work requirements.

notes:
Healthcare: 2019 statements vary between 'Medicare for All is the obvious solution' and support for a public option while keeping private insurance; the public-option framing is his later and clearer position. Official House website (swalwell.house.gov), congress.gov, GovTrack, Ballotpedia and his campaign site were unreachable or empty, so several answers rest on secondary compilations (OnTheIssues) at medium or low confidence. No 2026 debate transcripts or platform text were found. Stated positions only; no inference.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 34 answers taken from it, 9 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass, without copying existing answers. All 490 statements and remaining nulls reviewed. Saved the seventeen Swalwell-only FOX questionnaire sections, all twenty-one disability questionnaire answers, the complete CNN town hall and ABC interview, and the original religion-podcast transcript. Speaker labels and context exclude guests, hosts, advertisements and other candidates. His March 2026 public-option answer clarifies the older single-payer/public-option wording. Community-college tuition is distinguished from unconditional free four-year education. His congressional service ended April 14, 2026; the questionnaire host records his April 13 campaign suspension. An official Ethics Committee investigation announcement was downloaded; allegations and resignation do not establish particular quiz positions, and his denials are not treated as exoneration. His closed House domain prevented retrieving some older releases. A 2025 Gaza letter located during research did NOT include him among its four signatories, so none of its positions were attributed to him. His actual 2023 jointly led letter was read on coauthor Raskin’s original site. Regional development proposals are not treated as a universal global-aid duty; support for two states does not establish every nation’s right to separate statehood. Iran internet legislation is a proposal, not enacted law; secure messaging is not assumed to answer the broader unbreakable-encryption statement. Fusion research testimony was read in full; research support does not establish a position on expanding existing nuclear power, and the contrary 2019 quotation in a tertiary compilation could not be traced to its blocked original. AI safeguards do not establish a general view on technological acceleration or human extinction. Cannabis reform is not legalization of all drugs. Christian identity and interfaith experience do not establish positions on blasphemy, apostasy, theological doctrine, or interfaith marriage. Nonviolence is not inferred from state criminal sentencing. Cosponsorship and voting remain medium, as does rhetoric. No inferred answers; inclusion-only rejection is accepted. Later pass 2026-11-14 (claude-sonnet-5-5): his House roll calls (2013-2026) are now cited and replace the OnTheIssues compilation, which only reports his votes secondhand; five OnTheIssues-only answers whose originals could not be found or did not say it were nulled, and two (school-vouchers, surveillance-ok) were answered from his roll calls. Themes searched by vote: economy, government, society, liberty, ecology, world.
